$comment: PERMISSION MODE. The routines here run unattended in an ephemeral cloud container on a
schedule, with no human in the session. A permission prompt in that setting has nobody to
answer it, so the run does not fail, it WEDGES: it holds the container open until the
container is reclaimed, and the day's work is lost with no error anyone sees. bypassPermissions
is what keeps an unattended run finishing. It is not the thing containing the blast radius.
The containment is ownership.yaml, the CI guards, and the fact that docs/ is regenerated
rather than edited: a run can only write inside its own lane, and only a maintainer session
can change what the lanes are. Owner decision, 2026-08-11.
THE MODE WAS NEVER THE THING STILL ASKING. On 2026-08-20 the owner was interrupted twice by
an unattended run stopping for approval, with this file already setting bypassPermissions and
having set it for nine days. A session that goes looking at the permission mode finds it
correct and loses the afternoon, so the answer is written here where it will be looked for.
What asks is the Bash SANDBOX, which is a separate mechanism from the permission mode. A
sandboxed command that writes outside the working tree cannot complete, and the tool then
asks to re-run it unsandboxed. That is a prompt bypassPermissions does not cover, and the run
had been writing its scratch scripts into a system temp directory all morning.
The cure is not a broader permission. It is to stop leaving the tree: every scratch file goes
in out/<run>/tmp/, which is gitignored and inside the working directory, so nothing needs
escaping and nothing needs approving. That rule is in CLAUDE.md, because it is a rule about
how the routines work and not a setting. Owner decision, 2026-08-20.
The allow list below is belt and braces. bypassPermissions already covers it, and it is
written out so that a session running under a HOST that overrides the mode, which the cloud
runner may do, still has the tools this routine cannot finish without.
THE ACTOR STAMP IS NAMED HERE, on the owner's instruction, 2026-08-26. Phase 17 writes
.git/ACTOR twice in every run, once to hand the retro its narrow lane and once to hand it
back, and both writes were prompting. .git/ is inside the working tree and outside what the
Bash sandbox will write to, so the scratch rule in CLAUDE.md does not reach it: there is no
other place to put the stamp, because the commit-msg hook reads it from exactly that path.
The approval that was granted on the day landed in .claude/settings.local.json as two exact
command strings, which is gitignored, dies with the container, and misses any variation of
the command. So it is written here, where it survives a fresh clone.
This GRANTS NOTHING the ownership map does not already govern. The stamp is a label a commit
wears, not a permission: writing 'upgrade' into it does not widen what may be written, it
NARROWS it, and ownership_check and the pre-commit hook both read the map rather than the
stamp. A run that stamped itself 'human' would still be refused on every human-owned path.

hooks.command: python3 -c "import importlib,subprocess,sys; need=[p for m,p in [('yaml','pyyaml'),('requests','requests')] if not importlib.util.find_spec(m)]; subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','pip','install','--break-system-packages','-q',*need]) if need else None" 2>/dev/null || true
